title: Grateful Dead Live at Oregon State University on 1970-01-17
lineage: Master Soundboard Reel > DAT > CDR > SHN

ai_review.summary: Solid early‑'70 soundboard capture with a funky Hammond organ and strong performances of Good Lovin', The Eleven, Dark Star and other classics, despite occasional distortion and a slight pitch slowdown.
ai_review.review: The show is widely praised for its energetic early‑1970 vibe, highlighted by standout renditions of Good Lovin', Mason’s Children, High Time, St. Stephen → The Eleven, Dark Star and Lovelight, plus an unusually funky Hammond organ tone. The soundboard source is generally listenable but suffers from occasional distortion, mediocre balance in places, a noticeable half‑step pitch slowdown and some splice artifacts.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers (9 of 14) rate the performance 4–5 stars, noting many standout songs; recording issues are mentioned but not enough to outweigh the strong musical content.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Slight distortion and mediocre balance in spots, a half‑step pitch slowdown, occasional dropouts/splices; overall clear enough for enjoyment.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers describe a tight early‑'70 set that builds momentum, with a powerful second half featuring seamless transitions (e.g., St. Stephen into The Eleven) and high‑energy jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his guitar tone and being “on” that night; noted for cutting loose during Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Keys: Funky Hammond organ with a ’67 feel, sourced from a Baptist church, giving the show a unique texture.
